source.title: The Funduk
source.summary: From makhzan to magazine: the trade infrastructure that connected three continents.
source.author: Islamic Economics
source.body_text: The word "magazine" comes from the Arabic makhzan, meaning warehouse. Step inside the medieval funduk, the complete trade ecosystem with warehouses, lodging, money changers, and translators. Explore the 3,000-strong caravanserai network, the waqf endowments that funded public infrastructure, and how Venice's fondaco district was inspired by Islamic institutional design.

x.single_post: Most people think warehouses are about storing goods. They are actually about moving trust across impossible distances. A merchant in Baghdad could cash a cheque in Canton.
thread: Most people think warehouses are about storing goods. They are actually about moving trust across impossible distances.
The Arabic word makhzan became our word "magazine." Step inside the medieval funduk: warehouse, hotel, bank, and translation service under one roof.
Three thousand caravanserai connected three continents. Each one was a complete trade ecosystem funded by waqf endowments.
Venice's fondaco district copied this Islamic institutional design. The architecture of global commerce was born in the medieval Muslim world. https://islamiceconomics.github.io/podcast.html#ep-tt-4

linkedin.post: The word "magazine" traces back to the Arabic makhzan, meaning warehouse. But these weren't just storage facilities. The medieval funduk was a complete trade ecosystem: warehouse, lodging, money exchange, and translation services under one roof. Picture 3,000 caravanserai forming a network that connected three continents. What made this remarkable wasn't just the scale—it was the trust infrastructure. Waqf endowments funded public trade infrastructure. Venice's fondaco district was directly inspired by this Islamic institutional design. A merchant in Baghdad could cash a cheque in Canton, 4,000 miles away, on reputation alone. The architecture of global commerce was born in the medieval Muslim world. Listen: https://islamiceconomics.github.io/podcast.html#ep-tt-4
